verifications.claim: The Artemis 2 mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026... hit the water at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego on April 10 just past 8 p.m. EDT / 5 p.m. PDT'; R3: 'splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R4: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego, expected around 5 p.m. Pacific time'; R5: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego... at 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, timezone conversion, location, and successful splashdown.

Integrity and its four astronauts'; R2: 'Orion “Integrity” spacecraft’s four-person crew'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen' (lists four); R5: 'her crew of four astronauts'

verifications.reasoning: Sources describe it as the first crewed mission to the moon vicinity and return since Apollo 17 (over 50 years), directly supporting the claim despite flyby trajectory.
